campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a new interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, along with public hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permits for two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application for public works funding and approving consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation, replacing a prior interim ordinance
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization for the Public Works Director to submit a One Bay Area Grant application
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — June 3, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered several service level options proposed by the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office for providing law enforcement services in the upcoming fiscal year. Council members were asked to choose which staffing/service option to pursue and offer direction on the city's near-term approach to its Sheriff's contract.
keyTopics: Selecting a Sheriff's Office service level option for FY 2026 contract
Council direction on the city's near-term approach to Sheriff staffing

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business including meeting minutes, financial reports, and payment records, and considered appointing a voting delegate for an upcoming League of California Cities conference. The Council also took up an ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code and considered amending a professional services agreement, along with a request related to a public hearing on appeals.
keyTopics: Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026
Appointment of voting delegate and alternate for the League of California Cities Annual Conference
Omnibus ordinance amending the Town Code with minor updates
Second amendment to an existing professional services agreement
Request to continue or hear a public hearing on appeals

san-jose.title: San José City Council — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was a procedural City Council meeting focused on setting the agenda for upcoming meetings. The Council reviewed the final agenda for the September 1, 2026 meeting, considered a public record covering mid-August, and took up a VEBA Advisory Committee appointment along with a joint special meeting involving the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 1, 2026 City Council agenda, including any new items and time-certain scheduling
Cancellation of the review of the draft agenda for the September 8, 2026 meeting
The public record covering August 13-20, 2026
A VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
A joint special meeting with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council held a closed session to discuss performance evaluations and labor negotiations involving two of its directly appointed employees, the City Clerk and City Manager. The meeting also included a general public comment period for topics not otherwise on the agenda.
keyTopics: Closed-session performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiations discussion involving the City Clerk and City Manager, with Vice Mayor Clark as the city's designated negotiator
Public comment period for non-agenda items

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held two special meetings: an early closed-session meeting where members met privately on confidential matters, followed by a later public meeting featuring a presentation on the Clean Water Program update.
keyTopics: Closed session meeting (details confidential)
Clean Water Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss plans for an upcoming Bike Fest event and a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program, as well as a presentation from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI. The Commission also considered approval of minutes from its June 10, 2026 meeting and held a general public comment period.
keyTopics: Bike Fest event planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Presentation from youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing both in-person and remote participation. Councilmember Chahal joined remotely from Panchkula, India, and the agenda excerpt provided does not include details on specific policy items considered.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format with in-person and Zoom/phone options for public participation

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered introducing an ordinance to amend a section of the city's municipal code and received an educational presentation on the basics of municipal bonds from the Finance Department. The meeting also included routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and reviewing upcoming agenda items.
keyTopics: Ordinance to amend Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapters B.6
Presentation: 'Municipal Bonds 101' from Finance Department staff
City Council calendar of upcoming meetings
Approval of City Council meeting minutes
Preview of anticipated items for the next regular Council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission reviewed a public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real private development, with a presentation from the project's art consultant and artist team. The Commission also considered funding for a temporary interactive media art installation series and the donation of artworks by two local artists to the city's collection.
keyTopics: Approval of June 18, 2026 Public Art Commission meeting minutes
Final review of the public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real development, with presentations by art consultant Danielle Wohl, artist Giles Miller, and Acclaim Companies
Allocation of up to $70,000 from the Art in Public Places fund for Code:ART 2027 interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei into the city's public art collection
